, at present, we do not know how to reconcile our results with the ADS/CFT conjecture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the absence of physical matter flux, all conserved quantities of asymptotically ADS spacetimes must vanish.
the asymptotically anti-de-Sitter boundary conditions are consistent with the ADS/CFT dictionery only in the sense that the boundary theory can be viewed as an effective theory.
, if the ADS/CFT conjecture holds in the fully non-pertubative regime, it must be a highly non-trivial generalization of the one currently proposed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the `boundary conditions' for asymptotically ADS spacetimes are not as trivial as they might appear to be at first sight.
the `conservation of charges' is a necessary, but not sufficient, requirement for a theory to have a sensible asymptotically anti-de-Sitter limit.
the `boundary stress tensor' in d dimensions is not a tensor.
